slides.heading: Middle Node
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Easy · Linked Lists
slides.narration: Let's solve Middle Node, an easy linked lists problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Return the middle node (second middle for even lengths) via slow/fast pointers.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Return the middle node (second middle for even lengths) via slow or fast pointers.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: A fast pointer moving two steps lands at the end exactly when a slow pointer moving one step reaches the middle.
slides.narration: A fast pointer moving two steps lands at the end exactly when a slow pointer moving one step reaches the middle.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Two passes: count length, then walk n/2 → O(n)
Or copy into an array → O(n) space
One pass: slow/fast pointers → O(n), O(1) space
slides.narration: You could count the length and then walk half of it, which takes two passes, or copy the nodes into an array. The slow and fast pointer trick finds the middle in one pass with constant space.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Start slow and fast at the head
2. Advance slow by one, fast by two
slides.narration: Step by step. First, start slow and fast at the head. Second, advance slow by one, fast by two. Third, stop when fast runs out. Fourth, return slow.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: slow and fast start at the head
slides.narration: Both pointers start at the head, the node with value two.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: slow → 7, fast → 3
slides.narration: Slow moves one step to 7; fast moves two steps to 3.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: slow → 3, fast → 9
slides.narration: Slow moves one step to 3; fast moves two steps to 9.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: fast can't move: middle is 3
slides.narration: Fast is at the last node, so slow is at the middle: 3.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: Slow and fast start at the head. While fast and fast dot next aren't null, slow moves one step and fast moves two. Return slow.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is constant.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Even length: return the SECOND middle
Check fast and fast.next before moving
slides.narration: For an even length, the problem wants the second middle node, which this loop naturally returns. Always check fast and fast dot next before jumping.

bullets: A fast pointer moving two steps lands at the end exactly when a slow pointer moving one step reaches the middle.
